s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules on the face and vulva
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Approximately 60 lesions are present
Lesions are located on the face and vulva
Medical history includes a meningioma
Family history includes a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology of lesions shows basaloid cells and small cystic spaces
Genetic testing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

differentials: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
per_call: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

shortlist.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches basaloid cells and cystic spaces in histopathology, and SUFU gene mutation

shortlist.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with multiple skin-colored papules and basaloid cells in histopathology

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches histopathologic features of basaloid cells and small cystic spaces

shortlist.label: Gorlin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Associated with basal cell carcinomas and genetic mutations, although specific SUFU mutation is more indicative of NBCCS

shortlist.label: Bazex-Dupre-Christol syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by multiple basal cell carcinomas, although less commonly associated with SUFU gene mutations

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, along with a history of meningioma and a family history of similar lesions, is consistent with Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome. The histopathology showing basaloid cells and small cystic spaces, as well as the genetic testing revealing a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
rejected.why: While this condition also presents with basaloid follicular hamartomas, the presence of a meningioma and the specific genetic mutation in the SUFU gene are more characteristic of Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a type of basal cell carcinoma, but it does not account for the patient's family history or the genetic mutation found in the SUFU gene.

rejected.label: Gorlin syndrome
rejected.why: Gorlin syndrome is another name for Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.

rejected.label: Bazex-Dupre-Christol syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with follicular atrophoderma, hypotrichosis, and basal cell carcinomas, but it does not typically involve the vulva or have the same genetic mutation as Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.
